thread:
Maria P: Quick sync — Datadog + HW partner (BlueChipHW) want a joint announcement about GPU inference observability. Need to align on dashboards, OTLP spans, and a marketplace tile. Who can own dashboard artifacts?
Alex M: I can do the dashboard layout + sample queries. want to confirm metric names and span attributes first.
Sara O: From partnerships side we need a simple demo that shows latency + cost/unit improvements when using Redwood caching. Short and visual.
Dan E: For traces we should standardize these tags: service=redwood-inference, model.name, model.version, gpu.id, seq_len, token_count, latency_ms, cache.hit=true/false. Also add redwood.request_id for trace linking.
Maria P: @Dan E that list is perfect. Can you add the OTLP mapping snippet? Datadog engineering asked for explicit attribute names.
Dan E: Pasting a quick OTLP mapping example we plan to include in the repo:
```json
{
  "resource": {"service.name": "redwood-inference"},
  "spans": [
    {"name": "generate_tokens", "attributes": {"model.name":"gpt-3-redwood","model.version":"v1","gpu.id":"gpu-4","sequence_len":256,"latency_ms":45}}
  ]
}
```
Maria P: Nice. DatadogBot just pinged me with initial integration docs link: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/otlp-redwood (shared by partner). They want to map our cache metrics into their 'apm' views.
Alex M: For the dashboard: top row = trace latency (95th/50th), traces per minute, cache hit rate. Middle row = GPU utilization heatmap by pod, model throughput. Bottom = cost per 1k tokens + rollout comparison. I'll mock queries using Datadog metrics: redwood.latency_ms.p95, redwood.traces.per_min, redwood.cache.hit_rate.
Sara O: Partner will provide a sample ML workload and test data on Wed. We should schedule a run Thursday to capture stable metrics.
Dan E: Tests we need: 1) high-concurrency burst 2) long sequence (>=2048) 3) cache warm vs cold 4) failover to fallback model. We should tag traces with scenario: test.scenario.
Maria P: Ops ask: ensure dashboard doesn't expose sensitive customer IDs. Use model.name+env tags only. Also need copy for joint blog + marketplace tile.
Alex M: I'll create the dashboard in our Datadog sandbox and export JSON. Will add widget notes for the marketing copy. Plan: dashboard draft by Tue EOD.
Sara O: I'll draft the joint blog outline and PRF for BlueChipHW approvals. Need a short blurb about observability benefits (cost/latency) and a CTA to the marketplace listing.
DatadogBot: New integration checklist item added: "trace/span attribute convention review" — https://app.datadog.com/dash/checks/84732
Dan E: Small technical ask: for GPU metrics, prefer names like redwood.gpu.utilization and redwood.gpu.memory_used_mb. Partner exporters sometimes use different names; we'll add a translation layer in the agent.
Maria P: Action items: 
- Dan E: finalize OTLP attribute docs + example (due: Tue 11:59 PT)
- Alex M: dashboard draft + export (due: Tue EOD)
- Sara O: blog outline + partner approvals (initial draft Mon)
- Maria P: coordinate PR wording and marketplace tile copy (due: Wed)
Sara O: I'll block a 30m sync Mon 10:30 PT to review dashboard mock and blog outline. Invite BlueChipHW and Datadog eng.
Alex M: One more: include a small trace sample in the announcement (span waterfall) — I'll attach a .har/trace file to the dashboard export.
Dan E: For validation we should run these automated traces: `curl -H "x-redwood-test: bluechip-demo" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — will post a short script in the repo.
Maria P: Sounds good. If we hit blockers on metrics names, fallback is to use a mapping table in the marketplace tile README. Keep communications in this thread.
Sara O: :thumbsup: Thanks all — will send calendar invite and initial draft in this thread before Monday.
Alex M: FYI tagging: dashboards will be under folder "marketplace-integrations/bluechiphw-datadog".
Dan E: Quick note for infra: ensure GPU exporter has OTLP batch size >= 50 to avoid missing spans on high throughput.
Maria P: Closing note — priority is clarity for customers: one-click install + prebuilt dashboard + trace walkthrough. We'll iterate on visuals after the first run.
